traumavision.label: Thesis · UNC Córdoba · 2026
traumavision.title: TraumaVision AI
traumavision.subtitle: Clinical Decision Support for Pediatric Wrist Fractures on X-Rays
traumavision.description: Academic prototype: a YOLOv8m detector inside a FastAPI web app that marks the likely fracture site and issues a PDF report. Thesis internal test set (3,038 images): 96.7% sensitivity, 93.1% specificity. External test without retraining (PediURF): 97.4% / 88.3%. Now scaling through Emprende U 2026.
traumavision.led_line: Web app for AI-based pediatric wrist fracture detection
traumavision.pipeline: DICOM → CLAHE → YOLOv8m → Detection → PDF report
traumavision.problem: The thesis set out to build a second reader for pediatric wrist X-rays: a system that marks the likely fracture site on the image while the physician keeps the decision. Scope: pediatric wrist only (patients up to 19), frontal or lateral view, conventional radiography.
traumavision.role: Author of the capstone project (Proyecto Integrador, UNC), with two UNC advisors. I built the data pipeline, trained and evaluated the model, developed the web app and wrote the regulatory analysis.

decisions.title: Drop the classifier, switch to detection.
decisions.body: An earlier DenseNet-121 classifier had data leakage and relied on the lead L/R markers instead of the bone, so its figures were discarded and the project moved to a YOLOv8m detector that boxes each finding.

decisions.title: Split by patient.
decisions.body: GRAZPEDWRI-DX (20,327 images from 6,091 patients) was split 70/15/15 by patient, so no patient appears in both training and test.

decisions.title: Fix the threshold before the test.
decisions.body: The decision threshold (0.22) was set on the validation set, as the highest value that kept image-level sensitivity at 96% or more, before the first test run.

decisions.title: Test on data from another country.
decisions.body: The final model ran without retraining on PediURF, a pediatric dataset from Shenzhen, China (1,000 cases, 1,790 images).

traumavision.result: Internal test set (3,038 images, 914 unseen patients): 96.7% sensitivity, 93.1% specificity and AUC-ROC 0.987 per image; box mAP@50 0.944. External test (PediURF): 97.4% sensitivity and 88.3% specificity per image. Evaluated on retrospective data; not registered with ANMAT or authorized for clinical use. Code public under AGPL-3.0. Now scaling through Emprende U 2026; extending it to other regions requires expert-labeled datasets.

kibbo.led_line: Bilingual website and SEO/GEO for a hospital-equipment maintenance platform
kibbo.eyebrow: Case Study · B2B SaaS · Built via Eleven · 2026
kibbo.title: KIBBO
kibbo.subtitle: Bilingual website and SEO/GEO for a hospital-equipment CMMS.
kibbo.problem: KIBBO is a CMMS (computerized maintenance management system) for hospital medical equipment. The product worked, but kibbo.io ran an outdated WordPress site that did not explain it and throttled search crawlers. A biomedical engineer evaluating KIBBO could not see the product running or check who already uses it.
kibbo.role: Through Eleven, I led design, front-end development, SEO/GEO and the English edition. The build ran on our AI-agent pipeline, with my review and sign-off at every checkpoint.

decisions.title: Write to the technician, not the buyer.
decisions.body: Third person, no promotional claims, and every statement backed by a real product screen, because the reader is the person who will operate it every day.

decisions.title: Keep KIBBO and LEEX apart.
decisions.body: Figures from the hardware manufacturer are credited to LEEX, so the KIBBO site claims only what KIBBO can back.

decisions.title: Give mobile its own system.
decisions.body: "Expediente" (case file) lays out each page as a record instead of compressing the desktop scroll into a phone.

decisions.title: Make English a full edition.
decisions.body: Own slugs, reciprocal hreflang and the Spanish canonical kept intact; user quotes stay verbatim in Spanish with a labeled translation, so no one is misquoted.

kibbo.result: Live on kibbo.io in Spanish and English, replacing the legacy WordPress site, with GA4 measuring from launch.
seo_items: JSON-LD: Organization, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage; ratings only where visible.
Reciprocal ES/EN hreflang, x-default and a canonical per language.
Sitemap built from one route registry, dated by real edits.
Citable guides: CMMS explainer, tender checklist, country records (ES).

leex.led_line: Web app for public tender detection and AI-drafted bid verdicts
leex.eyebrow: Case Study · Internal B2B System · LEEX · 2026
leex.title: LEEX Tender System
leex.subtitle: Detects public tenders across 33 sources and drafts bid verdicts for sales.
leex.problem: LEEX, an Argentine medical equipment company, sells mainly through public tenders. Tenders are published across dozens of government portals, each with its own format and deadlines. A tender detected late cannot be bid on, and bidding requires checking each requirement against the product sheet. The previous tool was a single-user script feeding a spreadsheet.
leex.role: I led it end to end: scoped it with sales and management, designed the architecture, and built the engine and the web app with a pipeline of AI coding agents under my direction.

decisions.title: Code before AI.
decisions.body: A deterministic dictionary-plus-vector match filters first, and an LLM evaluates only what passes, which keeps the system cheap, testable and explainable.

decisions.title: A person signs every verdict.
decisions.body: The model drafts a requirement-by-requirement case citing the tender and the product sheet, and sales decides, because a missed tender costs more than a review.

decisions.title: Three sweep states, not two.
decisions.body: "Nothing there", "couldn't see" and "saw far less than usual", because a portal that failed silently would otherwise look the same as one with no tenders.

decisions.title: Public first.
decisions.body: The engine reads each portal's public view and logs in only as a documented last resort, which reduced credential exposure and let the build start without waiting on access.

leex.result: In development, launch pending. It runs internally on real data: the first full pass went from sweep to triage to human-signed verdicts. Next step: rollout to the sales team.

b6_story.title: Where the incubator came from
b6_story.caption: In 1878, a Paris obstetrician had a zoo's poultry incubator adapted for newborns; with controlled heat alone, premature mortality fell from 66% to 38%. LEEX's B6 incubator builds on the same idea.

mri_explainer.title: How an MRI works
mri_explainer.caption: MRI uses no camera and no X-rays. Hydrogen nuclei in the body's water align in a strong magnetic field; a radio pulse at their resonance frequency excites them, and gradient coils encode position so the returning signal can be reconstructed as an image. Script researched from 20 institutional sources.
